name: GitLab Issues
summary: GitLab Issues sits in the same application as the code, so commits and merge requests can close issues. Statuses beyond open and closed need the Premium plan at $29 per user per month, billed annually. The Free plan allows 5 users in a private top-level group.

facts.text: Statuses such as In progress, Done or Won't do give finer tracking than open and closed, and the documentation lists statuses as a Premium and Ultimate feature.
Issues have no dedicated priority field in the documentation we read. Labels can carry relative priorities, and issue lists sort by an issue's highest-priority label.
A keyword such as Closes or Fixes before an issue reference in a commit message or merge request description closes the issue when it reaches the default branch.
Health status, which tracks delivery risk on each issue, is listed for the Ultimate plan.
The 5-user limit on the Free plan applies to private top-level groups on GitLab.com. It does not apply to public groups or paid tiers.

plans.name: Free
plans.notes: GitLab.com, 5 users per private top-level group, 400 compute minutes a month
